relevant_block.original_bytes:
do   -- garbage collection with no extra memory
  local L = T.newstate()
  T.loadlib(L, 1 | 2, 0)   -- load _G and 'package'
  local res = (T.doremote(L, [[
    _ENV = _G
    assert(string == nil)
    local a = {}
    for i = 1, 1000 do a[i] = 'i' .. i end    -- grow string table
    local stsize, stuse = T.querystr()
    assert(stuse > 1000)
    local function foo (n)
      if n > 0 then foo(n - 1) end
    end
    foo(180)    -- grow stack
    local _, stksize = T.stacklevel()
    assert(stksize > 180)
    a = nil
    T.alloccount(0)
    collectgarbage()
    T.alloccount()
    -- stack and string table could not be reallocated,
    -- so they kept their sizes (without errors)
    assert(select(2, T.stacklevel()) == stksize)
    assert(T.querystr() == stsize)
    return 'ok'
  ]]))
  assert(res == 'ok')
  T.closestate(L)
end

span.original_bytes:
An object is considered @def{dead}
as soon as the collector can be sure the object
will not be accessed again in the normal execution of the program.
(@Q{Normal execution} here excludes finalizers,
which resurrect dead objects @see{finalizers},
and it excludes also some operations using the debug library.)
Note that the time when the collector can be sure that an object
is dead may not coincide with the programmer's expectations.
The only guarantees are that Lua will not collect an object
that may still be accessed in the normal execution of the program,
and it will eventually collect an object
that is inaccessible from Lua.
(Here,
@emph{inaccessible from Lua} means that neither a variable nor
another live object refer to the object.)
Because Lua has no knowledge about @N{C code},
it never collects objects accessible through the registry @see{registry},
which includes the global environment @see{globalenv} and
the main thread.

public_contract_sources.interpretation: Reachable objects survive; inaccessible objects are eventually collected. This is a public safety/liveness obligation, independent of bucket capacities.

span.original_bytes:
Although strings are subject to garbage collection,
they do not have an explicit construction and
their equality is by value;
they behave more like values than like objects.
Therefore, they are not removed from weak tables.

public_contract_sources.interpretation: Strings compare by value and are not removed from Lua weak tables. A Lua weak-value table holding strings is not a valid oracle for weak intern-index reclamation.

span.original_bytes:
When @id{nsize} is zero,
the allocator must behave like @id{free}
and then return @id{NULL}.

When @id{nsize} is not zero,
the allocator must behave like @id{realloc}.
In particular, the allocator returns @id{NULL}
if and only if it cannot fulfill the request.

public_contract_sources.interpretation: Free releases existing storage; a nonzero request may fail. Preserve actual failure handling and do not equate a private resize attempt with a promised public capacity.
The actual explicit full collection remains required under the real test provider; private size observations cannot replace running it.

native_implementation.finding: The no-argument T helper reads G(L)->strt.size and nuse directly; indexed mode walks a private hash bucket and pushes actual TString entries. This is private test instrumentation, not a standard Lua/C API.
Shrink rehashes the old chains before attempting replacement allocation, and failure restores the original chain geometry. Capacity equality checks this C-specific rollback, not merely successful GC.
Ordinary full GC can request a string-table shrink when usage falls below one quarter; emergency collection omits it.

Short strings reuse equal live headers, revive unswept dead headers and increment private population on creation. Live content/identity and safe revival are useful counterparts; exact nuse is not a public count contract.
Native test countlimit0 rejects every unequal nonzero resize, including shrink; frees remain allowed. Do not describe it as a growth-only control.

ada_implementation.finding: Allocate the complete replacement index before relinking actual weak chains. Refusal may run emergency collection against the old valid index. The current implementation grows the index and does not shrink it during collection; equal retained capacity alone would be a trivial insufficient counterpart.

Ordinary <=40-byte strings use actual weak header chains; hits revive the header and may add an allocation-free transient operation root. Binary byte equality, live identity and root lifetime remain required.
Actual release unlinks the interned header and decrements the Ada population before disposal. No permanent strong cache may replace this lifetime.
Actual unreachable managed objects are released by the shared collector. Selected-owner final disposal and retry must remain honest.

Current Ada conformance count/byte controls reject growth, not native unequal-size shrink. This packet does not approve that wider provider semantic difference; counterpart refusal coverage must identify an actual attempted growth and refusal.
The current child-state T module does not install querystr. No proposal may substitute a constant or label a missing/omitted private call as passing C API evidence.
